sections.html:
Jasper is small and rural. Monticello, the county seat, is the lone city, and Shady Dale is the lone town. The county covers 373 square miles. Public education is a four-school system that includes Jasper County High School.

Population is 17,632 as of mid-2025, up 20.8% from the 2020 count, where the prior decade added only 4.9%. Anyone buying acreage is likely to raise questions on wells, septic and frontage, so have that information ready if you are listing land.

Owners live in 85.6% of occupied homes here. Across 2020 to 2024 the middle owned home was worth $243,400, middle rent ran $970 monthly and middle household income was $60,134. Count 7,118 housing units, with 124 permits pulled in 2025.

Owner costs run $1,461 a month with a mortgage and $480 without. Commutes average 39.2 minutes, which shows how far the Atlanta metro area pulls. In 2020, 13.7% of the 6,270 housing units were vacant. Compare those carrying costs with the $243,400 middle value when you set an asking price.

sections.h2: Which office answers which tax question
sections.html:
Several hands touch a bill before it reaches you, and the Tax Commissioner's are the last. The commission and school board set millage. The assessors set value. A Grand Jury appointed board rules on disputes. The commissioner mails and collects.

  • Tax Commissioner: 126 W. Greene Street, Suite 125, Monticello, GA 31064; (706) 468-4902; counter open Monday through Friday, 8 to 4:30.
  • Tax Assessor: signs off on exemptions and notifies owners when it changes a value.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: the courthouse deed room provides warranty deed copies.

One mill is a dollar per thousand of assessed value, and 40% of market value is the assessed figure.

sections.h2: When a Jasper County bill comes due
sections.html:
Under the usual schedule, land, buildings and business personal property are billed in two halves, due September 20 and December 20. Statewide, December 20 is the standard deadline, and interest holds off until two months after the bill is postmarked.

The 2026 notice departed from that schedule: mailing on October 16, a first installment dated November 20, and the balance dated December 20. Printed dates can differ from year to year, so the ones on your own statement win.

  • Manufactured housing: payment and a location permit by April 1 each year.
  • Missing it brings a 10% penalty and possibly a citation to Magistrate Court or sale of the unit.
  • Vehicles renew during the 30 days that end on the owner's birthday.

A lien often surfaces just as a sale nears closing. Once a bill sits unpaid beyond 90 days, the county records a tax FiFa at the Clerk of Superior Court and may levy on the property and sell it.

FiFa entries are open to the public, bureaus among them, and the tax office has no control over their use. Clear a recorded lien before closing.

Call (706) 468-4902 to get the balance. If your closing falls between the two installment dates, settle who pays each half and put that in the settlement papers.

  1. Call the commissioner for the current balance and any earlier years.
  2. Ask the Clerk of Superior Court whether a FiFa has been recorded against the parcel.
  3. Decide who pays each installment and write it into the settlement papers.
  4. Bring a copy of your deed, available from the courthouse deed room, if the title has any gaps.

A cash sale skips the lender's underwriting, which leaves tax payoff and lien release as the main items before the deed changes hands.

Every homestead gets two thousand dollars off assessed value. That cut applies to the county, school and State levies, though the portion of the rate paying off bonds is left out.

Apply at the Tax Commissioner's counter with a driver's license that shows your Jasper County address. Forms in hand by April 1 count for that year. Once approved, the exemption renews itself until you move, the title changes or you switch categories, and a larger local exemption takes the place of the State amount.

sections.h2: How to dispute a Jasper County value
sections.html:
Forty-five days is the limit, measured from the notice date. Take the case to the Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator. After either ruling, a written notice sent to the Board of Tax Assessors moves it to Superior Court.

Prepare ahead. During the January 1 to April 1 return period you can state your own opinion of market value, which gives you firm footing if the assessors change it later. Owners of mobile homes get 45 days to file with the assessors, plus 21 days after a change notice to reach the Board of Equalization.

If tax was charged or collected by mistake or unlawfully, ask in writing within three years of paying to get it back. A claim that grows out of an appealed value is paid after the final taxable value is settled.

City tax is a separate levy. Municipalities tax on their own, and the city clerk sends and collects that bill unless city and county have agreed on one combined bill. Vehicle tax is always collected by the county Tax Commissioner.

Holders of long-term notes secured by real estate must record them within 90 days, at the intangible recording rate of $1.50 per $500 of face amount or part of it.

The return season for taxable property runs January 1 through April 1. Skip it and the county simply carries forward last year's value and last year's real property exemptions.

Notices go to the last address on file, so report any move. Three programs change how land or buildings are valued.

  • Historic property: a building listed on the Georgia register, plus up to two acres around it, may qualify for preferential assessment.
  • Brownfield sites: land approved for cleanup can hold its value frozen for a decade.
  • Public safety survivors: a surviving spouse who has not remarried, of a firefighter or officer killed on duty, may be fully exempt once the agency's papers are filed.

If your property is in a program, the Board of Tax Assessors can say what a buyer must do to keep the status.

faqs.q: What is the street address for the Jasper County tax counter?
faqs.a: The counter is at 126 W. Greene Street, Suite 125, Monticello, GA 31064. Call (706) 468-4902. It opens weekdays, 8 to 4:30.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for a first Jasper County homestead claim?
faqs.a: April 1 of the first year you want the benefit. A later filing counts toward the following tax year, and you must have owned and lived in the home on January 1.

faqs.q: Does a Jasper County tax lien reach my credit file?
faqs.a: Possibly. Ninety days past due puts a FiFa lien on record with the Clerk of Superior Court, and those entries are public.

faqs.q: How do I get a Jasper County deed copy?
faqs.a: Visit the deed room of the Clerk of Superior Court in the Jasper County Courthouse.

faqs.q: What is the Jasper County appeal deadline?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the date on the assessment notice. After a ruling, written notice to the Board of Tax Assessors sends the case to Superior Court.
